title: A window host can report whether its last frame reached its intended output

needles: GPU health provider follows the window host's submission evidence

installed_sdk.rationale: Both queries are public virtuals on the installed WindowHost header, appended at the public vtable tail so a downstream subclass keeps its slot layout. A host that does not override them keeps the false default, so an SDK consumer that never implements them reports no evidence rather than a wrong claim. The delivery stays pending its installed-consumer proof.

offline_timeline_cli.rationale: No CLI verb, flag, handler, or accepted document shape changes. The queries are answered inside a live window host, which the offline timeline CLI never constructs.

offline_timeline_mcp.rationale: No MCP tool definition, schema entry, or handler changes. Nothing in tools/mcp reads a window host's frame outcome.

live_product_control.rationale: No capability, operation, executor binding, grant, or profile policy changes. The Development Inspector's existing gpu_submission_observed field gains a producer; the operation that reports it, its grants, and its profile policy are unchanged.

design_time_agent_manifest.rationale: docs/status/agent-capabilities.json is unchanged. A host reporting whether its last frame reached an output is runtime control plumbing, not a generator-facing design capability.
